title: R2 RESEARCH: reasoning-burden calibration for overruling - how high courts scale the justification burden to what is being overturned
description: Research remainder 2 of 2 from the addendum's agenda status (docs/serenissima-addendum-legal-theory.md section 8: "Item 3 (overruling doctrines): substantially advanced (section 3 corrective path + sources requirement); remaining: reasoning-burden calibration"), scoped by coordinator decision A8. The question is not WHETHER a system permits overruling but how it CALIBRATES the justification burden to what is being overturned. Cover at minimum: the statutory-vs-constitutional stare decisis asymmetry in US law (heightened deference for statutory precedent, e.g. Kimble v. Marvel Entertainment 576 U.S. 446 (2015); the special-justification requirement and the reliance-interest weighting in the Casey/Janus/Dobbs line), the UK 1966 Practice Statement's own caution about retrospective disturbance, the ECtHR/UK 'cogent reasons' framing, and the civil-law equivalents (Mexico: 'razones suficientes' / arts. 228-230 Ley de Amparo, sustitucion de jurisprudencia; Spain's interes casacional objetivo). Then calibrate for this harness: what burden should a corrective reinterpretation carry versus a valuation versus a full overruling. Output docs/precedent-research/11-reasoning-burden-calibration.md. Zero build dependency by construction.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE (create only this; touch no other file): docs/precedent-research/11-reasoning-burden-calibration.md. Do NOT create or edit docs/precedent-research/README.md - owned solely by the epic join T-362 (F1). Do NOT edit 01..09, either v0 synthesis document, PRECEDENT.md, INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, or anything under .harness/.

WEB RESEARCH IS REQUIRED: at least 5 named sources, at least 3 PRIMARY (judgment with case name and citation, statute or code article, official practice statement or court rule, or named-author treatise / peer-reviewed article). Final Sources section with retrievable identifiers. Parametric-only claims tagged SPECULATION.
EVERY substantive claim carries exactly one tag: ESTABLISHED / ANALOGY / SPECULATION. An untagged substantive claim is a defect and grounds for REJECT.

MANDATORY CALIBRATION TABLE, the document's centrepiece: one row per class of overturned thing (e.g. statutory interpretation, constitutional holding, a merely apparent ratio corrected on re-reading of sources, a force valuation such as declaring a passage obiter, an error-in-pronouncement claim, a context-change claim). Each row gives: the burden the system imposes, the mechanism that enforces it, the observable artifact the burden produces, and who checks it. A prose-only answer does not satisfy this criterion.

MAP THE BURDEN ONTO BOTH LADDERS EXPLICITLY: (a) the four D4 authority tiers, and (b) the three A4 operations - determination, reinterpretation (declarative / corrective-restrictive / corrective-extensive), valuation. State whether the burden should be a function of the TARGET'S TIER, of its FORCE under coordinator decision A2 (graded, raised by reiteration, decaying), or of its RELIANCE FOOTPRINT (how many later records cite it - the cited_by depth the registry already records). Pick one primary variable, name the others as modifiers, and justify from sources.

MUST ENGAGE SDR-07 DIRECTLY: docs/precedent-research/synthesis-design-requirements.md SDR-07 already ruled that tier-3 overruling requires EQUAL adversarial weight, not more. State whether your sources support equal-weight symmetry or a graded burden. If graded, name the grading variable and say precisely what SDR-07 would have to be amended to. Note that any such amendment is itself an act the layer must record - flag it for T-352.

MUST ANSWER THE SOURCES QUESTION THE ADDENDUM RAISES: addendum section 3 (DIRECTIVE) holds that a successor may argue the declared ratio was merely apparent ONLY by reinterpreting the SOURCE MATERIALS, with recorded reasoning, at sufficient authority - and that correction without sources is mere disagreement and invalid. Find the closest real-world analogues (what a court must show to hold an earlier ratio was per incuriam or merely apparent) and state whether the sources support this as a burden RULE, and how systems police it.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Implications for the agent harness': map findings onto task IDs, the three roles plus coordinator, the D4 tiers, the A2 force model and the A4 operations. For each finding, name the schema field, CLI flag, exit code or protocol rule it demands, or state that it demands none.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Extends, does not duplicate': address by name docs/precedent-research/03-overruling-doctrines.md (the v0 research on overruling conditions), PRECEDENT.md section 7 (the shipped overruling protocol: who may overturn what and the required reasoning record), SDR-17.8 (tier symmetry, which governs overrules and voids but deliberately NOT supersedes), and the factor-recitation rule already implemented in precedent.py. Say EXTENDS or DUPLICATE for each.
MANDATORY: state at least one finding that CUTS AGAINST the addendum or coordinator decisions A1-A8 where the sources support one; if none, say so explicitly and why.
NO CODE, no edits under .harness/, no edits to PRECEDENT.md or INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, no registry writes.

Three most schema-relevant findings, each with its tag:

1. F1 [ESTABLISHED + ANALOGY] -- Kimble v. Marvel Entertainment, 576 U.S. 446 (2015)'s
   statutory/constitutional stare-decisis asymmetry exposes a missing input in coordinator
   decision A2's force formula: A2 computes force from issuance tier + reiteration/decay only,
   with no variable for "does an external, non-precedent fix channel exist for the interpreted
   material" (a spec file an operator could just amend, vs. the precedent layer's own
   ontology, which only the overruling-grade protocol can ever fix). Kimble shows real doctrine
   grants heightened protection AT ISSUANCE for the former class, independent of citation count
   -- A2 as drafted cannot represent this. Flagged as a candidate 6th AMENDED/UNCHANGED item
   for T-352, classified as a reinterpretation-corrective-restrictive act if adopted.

2. F3 [ESTABLISHED + ANALOGY] -- the reasoning-CONTENT burden (factor-note specificity,
   --acknowledge-reliance) should be graded by the target's A2 force + cited_by reliance
   footprint, NOT by authority_tier; SDR-07's own quorum axis should stay UNCHANGED (Mexican
   art. 228/229 decoupling still supports equal adversarial weight for WHO may act), but 01's
   already-established US panel/en-banc asymmetry (overruling categorically needs MORE process
   than issuing new precedent) is real, sourced counter-evidence SDR-07 already named as a
   TRADEOFF and declined to resolve -- this document confirms that tension from an independent
   source rather than discovering it. Net: primary variable = force (with tier as a procedural-
   only modifier, reliance footprint as an independent escalation trigger) -- OPEN-QUESTION
   forwarded to T-352 for SDR-17.11/17.12, not enacted here (no code, no SDR edits, per this
   task's own scope).

3. F4 [ESTABLISHED + ANALOGY] -- Morelle Ltd v Wakeling [1955] 2 QB 379's per incuriam test
   ("ignorance or forgetfulness of some... authority binding on the court concerned... found...
   to be demonstrably wrong") gives A1's mandatory sources[] field (the addendum sec 3 DIRECTIVE)
   a concrete, mechanically checkable content rule for corrective reinterpretation acts: at
   least one sources[] entry must be a token NOT already present in the target record's own
   sources/cites -- the mechanical analogue of "not brought to the attention of the earlier
   court." Also flags, honestly, that the addendum's structured sources[] mandate is a STRICTER
   mechanism than any single doctrine surveyed requires (per incuriam is proven by argument, not
   a checklist) -- a qualification, not a contradiction, recorded per this task's instruction to
   report tensions even where the addendum is binding design input.
